# Booking portal: project brief

Harbour Clinics runs eleven small clinics and still books appointments by phone. The receptionists
spend most of the morning on the telephone, patients wait on hold, and about one appointment in
six is missed because nobody reminded the patient. This brief says what the new portal must do.

Patients must be able to book, move and cancel their own appointments online, at any hour, without
phoning anyone. A patient who has not booked before creates an account with an email address and
a password; no other details are needed until the first visit. Moving or cancelling is possible up
to two hours before the appointment, and after that the portal tells the patient to phone the clinic.

Every patient gets a text message the evening before an appointment and another two hours before
it. The message carries the clinic's address and a link to cancel. If the patient replies with
the word CANCEL the appointment is cancelled and the slot goes back on sale straight away.

Receptionists need one screen that shows a day's appointments for their clinic, with the free
slots, and they must be able to add a walk-in patient to a free slot in a few seconds. Clinic
managers need a monthly report of missed appointments for each clinic. Both screens are for staff
only and sit behind the clinic staff login.

Patient records are health data. The portal must keep them encrypted at rest and may only show a
patient their own appointments. Staff see only the clinic they work at, and every time a staff
member opens a patient record that is written to an access log that cannot be edited.

During the evening peak, between 17:00 and 20:00, about 300 patients an hour will be booking. The
portal has to keep every page under two seconds in that period and must not go down for planned
maintenance except between 02:00 and 04:00.

We have not decided on a payment step. Fees stay at the desk for now.
